AzurPilot Android brings AzurPilot to Android, with run controls, a virtual display preview, a native in-app interface, and logs. It supports arm64-v8a and x86_64 devices; the app and Runtime update separately, with multi-mirror multi-threaded Runtime downloads.

Whether the app runs well differs a lot between phones. Please add one entry — brand, model, system version, working or not — to the device support list on GitHub. Your single record saves others a lot of trial and error.

This app works with shizuku-m, a modified Shizuku that reconnects offline after every reboot without WLAN or a computer. It shares the official package name but uses a different signature, so it cannot be installed over the official build — uninstall the official Shizuku first, then install shizuku-m as prompted. Uninstalling it does not affect this app data.

Integrates seven keep-alive mechanisms — silent audio, 1px foreground overlay, companion device service, accessibility daemon, CPU wakelock, scheduled jobs and alarms, and a dual-process watchdog — against background termination.
Loops zero-volume silent audio in AudioFlinger to mark the process as an active media entity
Mounts a 1x1 transparent overlay to elevate process priority to visible window (requires overlay permission)
Holds a system Partial WakeLock to keep the CPU running and prevent deep sleep while screen is off
Combines system JobScheduler and AlarmManager to periodically wake up the process in Doze mode
Independent daemon process mutually monitors Binder death to resurrect each other, listening to boot and power events
Registers system companion device component for background execution and network exemptions
Leverages system accessibility service to automatically restart the process if terminated
